THE IDEA, SIMPLY

What happens after you click “check”?

Five small steps. No banking vocabulary required.

1

You enter a profile

Age, income, work history and existing EMIs—plus an optional credit score, amount and tenure.

2

We read public rules

Your values are compared with the official minimums and maximums captured for each lender.

3

You get reasons

Every pass or failure shows the applicant value, lender requirement and original source URL.

4

We compare costs

Where a starting rate is published, we estimate EMI and total interest for the same loan and tenure.

5

You get a shortlist

The strongest matches are ranked for further investigation—not presented as approved loan offers.

03 / CALCULATION

How is the screening calculated?

There is no trained approval model or secret customer dataset. This is an explainable public-rule screening engine.

ƒ
Applicant value + lender’s published requirement → pass, fail or unknown

For every selected lender, the engine compares your value with each hard rule captured from an official page. It shows the exact comparison and links back to that page.

ExampleAge 30 ≥ minimum age 21Result: rule passed
01
◷

Age

Your current age and, where published, your age when the requested loan tenure ends.

Example: age 57 + 4-year tenure = age 61 at closure.
02
◉

Employment type

Whether the product publicly supports salaried, self-employed, or both kinds of borrowers.

Example: a salaried-only product cannot be claimed for a business owner.
03
₹

Monthly income

Your take-home income compared with the lender’s published minimum income requirement.

Example: ₹30,000 passes a published ₹25,000 minimum.
04
↗

CIBIL score Optional

Your bureau score is checked only when you provide it and the lender publishes a numeric cut-off. “Ideal” scores stay advisory.

Blank score = unknown for that rule, never zero. Example: 700+ preferred is not an automatic rejection.
05
≋

Existing EMIs

Your current monthly debt payments. These reduce how much room remains for a new EMI.

Includes recurring loan and credit obligations—not normal living expenses.
06
%

FOIR

Fixed Obligation to Income Ratio: the share of monthly income allowed for all EMIs together.

₹80k income × 65% − ₹10k existing EMIs = ₹42k new-EMI room.
07
⌁

Work experience

Total time working and time with the current employer, checked separately when a lender publishes both.

Example: 24 months total and 12 months in the current job.
08
▦

Business vintage

For self-employed applicants, how long the business has operated when this rule is published.

Example: a lender may require two or three completed years.
09
◎

Lender relationship

Some products are only public for existing salary-account or pre-qualified customers.

The interface lets you include or exclude these relationship-only products.
10
↔

Amount and tenure

The requested amount and months are checked against product limits and maturity-age rules.

They also drive the FOIR-based amount calculation where possible.

Passes public rulesNo captured hard requirement failed. This is not a loan approval.

Insufficient public dataThe lender does not reveal enough stable information to decide.

How “best fit” is chosen

A fixed ranking order—not an unexplained score.

First pass the hard public rules. Then check whether the requested amount and tenure fit the public product limits. Prefer stronger evidence, and finally use the lower advertised starting rate as a cost tie-breaker.

  1. 1. Eligibility gateNo captured hard rule may fail.
  2. 2. Loan-fit gateRequested amount and tenure must fit public limits where known.
  3. 3. Evidence confidenceVerified → partial → conflict → insufficient.
  4. 4. Cost tie-breakerLower advertised starting rate ranks first.
Reducing-balance EMIP × r × (1+r)ⁿ ÷ ((1+r)ⁿ − 1)
Total interest(EMI × months) − principal
Illustrative interest differencecomparison interest − best-fit interest

The comparison uses the same principal and tenure and each lender’s advertised minimum rate. Processing fees, insurance, taxes, floating-rate changes and personalised pricing are excluded.

05 / METHOD

A decision trail, not a black box.

The prototype makes uncertainty visible instead of inventing precision.

01
⌁

Capture

Collect current criteria from official product pages, rate sheets, terms, FAQs and true eligibility calculators.

→
02
≡

Normalize

Turn age, income, work history, score and affordability language into typed, scoped rules.

→
03
◇

Screen

Test the profile against hard public rules. Soft guidance and conflicts never become automatic rejections.

→
04
↗

Explain

Return the rule outcome, source quality, advertised terms and what remains unknowable before application.

!
The honest boundary

Passing every captured public rule does not mean approval. Bureau details, fraud checks, employer categories, geography and internal scorecards may still change the lender’s decision.
